additional_info.subject: RE: ID0431054-DC/Si-D/MC-[Y2/R9 313202799060] Error Code “secc is offline CRM:02699000127
additional_info.body:
Dear Schoepff Cedric ,
Thanks for your response.
With the latest Sicharge D FW version, new OCPP VendorErrorCodes were introduced to enhance backend visibility. These codes reflect previously unreported communication losses and
do not indicate new or critical issues
.
"modbus0 is not connected"
: Brief 750ms loss of communication with SECC. No impact on charger performance, though rare cases may cause short outlet unavailability.
"secc is offline"
: Temporary CoAP polling error. SECC reconnects within 5 seconds. No performance impact.
These events have always occurred occasionally; the new FW simply logs them now. If such messages increase in frequency, a Hotfix with improved CoAP and Modbus handling can be installed.
Future FW versions will reduce non-impactful error reporting. We apologize for not informing CPOs earlier and will ensure future VendorErrorCodes are documented in Release Notes and Software Manuals.
The issue occurred only 2 times in our backend and lasted for approximately 5 seconds. Since the error has not reoccurred, it is not considered critical, and the charger is operating normally.
Please let us know if you have any further questions.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Ankita
Please do not change the subject of this Email when replying to it.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0431054-DC/Si-D/MC-[Y2/R9 313202799060] Error Code “secc is offline CRM:02699000127
additional_info.body:
Hello,
I completely understand the need for more detailed logs.
My criticism of this system is that the terminal has faults that are reported as “real” faults, and in our data analytics this is reflected in a drop in performance.
Then, on rarer occasions, the terminal remains in fault mode and requires a manual reboot.
Would it not be possible for errors that do not actually affect the proper functioning of the terminal to remain internal in the logs?
That way, I would not see anything in the OCPP field reports.
I would appreciate it if you could look into this issue because, even if it is not critical for you, it also has a negative impact on our customers.
Why is this?
When the terminal goes into error or becomes unavailable, our application treats it as a terminal that cannot be used, and therefore the customer will not come.
That is why I insist that no errors should be reported to the OCPP field if they do not interfere with the proper functioning of the terminal.
Thank you for your understanding of my request.
I look forward to hearing from you.
Best regards.
Cédric SCHOEPFF

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0431054-DC/Si-D/MC-[Y2/R9 313202799060] Error Code “secc is offline CRM:02699000127
additional_info.body:
Dear Schoepff Cedric ,
Following our analysis of the logs, we found two relevant events:
2025-06-16, 13:05:04
– The outlet was marked as out of order due to the charger not being in operating mode.
2025-06-16, 14:39:16
– An error occurred due to a SECC issue.
The first event is not considered critical, and the reboot was done only once when the outlet was out of order due to the EVSE not being in operating mode—not because of a SECC offline condition.
If you have observed similar issues at any other timestamps, please share them with us so we can investigate further.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Ankita
